lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: يُنفِقُونَ is in the derivative form: أَنْفَقَ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ن/ف/ق   n–f–q a desert rat’s tunnel, (of a desert rat) to go into 1 tunnel entrance and come out of another
; (of an animal) to die; to find a good market, to become depleted; to spend, to donate for a good cause, to support one’s family.

Of this root, 10 forms occur 111 times in the Qur’an:
نَافَقَ nāfaqa 2 times; أَنْفَقَ ʾanfaqa 68 times; نَفَقَة nafaqatun 2 times; نَفَقَاتٌ nafaqāt 1 time; إِنْفَاقٌ ʾinfāq 1 time; مُنْفِقُون munfiqūn 1 time; نِفَاقٌ nifāq 3 times; مُنَافِقُون munāfiqūn 27 times; مُنَافِقَاتٌ munāfiqāt 5 times and نَفَقٌ nafaq 1 time.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
أَنْفَقَ ʾanfaqa [v. IV trans.]

1 to spend (money)

(18:42) فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى مَا أَنْفَقَ فِيهَا so he began to wring his hands over what he had spent on it

2 to donate, to contribute, to give alms

(2:270) وَمَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ نَفَقَةٍ أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِنْ نَذْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُهُ whatever alms you donate or pledges you make, God surely knows it.

entries.label: مُنْفِقُون
entries.definitionHtml:
مُنْفِقُون munfiqūn [pl. of act. part. مُنْفِقٌ munfiq] ones who spend money in the way of God, donors

(3:17) الصَّابِرِينَ وَالصَّادِقِينَ وَالْقَانِتِينَ وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالأَسْحَارِ those who are steadfast, truthful, truly devout, who spend [in God’s cause] and those praying for forgiveness in the small hours of the night.

entries.label: نَافَقَ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَافَقَ nāfaqa [v. III trans., no object] to act hypocritically

(3:166) وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ نَافَقُوا and in order to mark out those who have been acting hypocritically.

entries.label: نَفَقٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَفَقٌ nafaq [n.] tunnel, passage through the earth

(6:35) فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقًا فِى الأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّمًا فِى السَّمَاءِ then if you can seek a tunnel into the ground or a ladder into the sky.

entries.label: إِنْفَاقٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
إِنْفَاقٌ ʾinfāq [v. n.] the act of spending money

(17:100) لَوْ أَنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزَائِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي إِذًا لأََمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ الإِنْفَاقِ if you possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, you would become tight‐fisted for fear of spending.

entries.label: مُنَافِقُونٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مُنَافِقُونٌ munāfiqūn [pl. of مُنَافِق munāfiq; fem. pl. مُنَافِِقات munāfiqāt] hypocrites

(57:13) يَوْمَ يَقُولُ الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا on the Day both male and female hypocrites will say to those who believed; * الْمُنَافِقُونَ name of Sura 63, Medinan sura, so‐named because of the reference in verses 1–

8 to the ‘Hypocrites’.

entries.label: نَفَقَةٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَفَقَةٌ nafaqatun [n., pl. نَفَقَاتٌ nafaqāt] charitable expenditure, donation, alms

(9:121) وَلاَ يُنْفِقُونَ نَفَقَةً صَغِيرَةً وَلاَ كَبِيرَةً وَلاَ يَقْطَعُونَ وَادِيًا إِلاَّ كُتِبَ لَهُمْ and they do not contribute donations either great or small, or traverse a valley, without it being recorded to them.

entries.label: نِفَاقٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نِفَاقٌ nifāq [v. n.; n.] hypocrisy, acting hypocritically

(9:97) الأَعْرَابُ أَشَدُّ كُفْرًا وَنِفَاقًا the desert Arabs are excessive in disbelief and hypocrisy.
